units.title: An eight-sided traffic sign has the meaning STOP.
A triangular traffic sign has the meaning YIELD.
A diamond-shaped warning identifies a special condition or hazard ahead and calls for slower, cautious travel.
Vertical rectangular signs generally give legal instructions or regulatory information.
Horizontal rectangular signs provide directions or other information.
A five-sided school sign marks a school zone or warns about a schoolchildren's crossing.
A pennant-shaped sign identifies a no-passing zone.
Crossbuck and circular railroad warnings call for looking both ways, listening and yielding to trains, with readiness to stop for an approaching train.
A number displayed below a crossbuck indicates that the crossing has multiple tracks.
Stop at flashing railroad lights and do not cross until the crossing is safe.
At a multiple-track crossing, watch for another train moving in either direction.
At a gated crossing, stop when the warning lights begin flashing rather than waiting for the gate to lower.
Remain stopped until the railroad gates have risen and the warning lights have stopped flashing.
Driving around a lowered railroad gate is dangerous and unlawful.
Regulatory signs state traffic-law requirements that drivers are expected to obey.
A red circle crossed by a slash prohibits the activity represented by its symbol.
A stop sign requires a full stop before entering the intersection.
Where a stop line is painted, stop at that line.
Stop before a crosswalk, whether or not the crossing is painted.
With no crosswalk, stop at the nearest safe point before the intersecting road where approaching traffic can be seen clearly.
At a yield sign, slow down and stop if needed to give crossing or merging traffic the right of way.
A speed-limit sign gives the maximum lawful roadway speed.
A No Left Turn sign prohibits a left turn.
A No Right Turn sign prohibits a right turn.
A No U-Turn sign prohibits a reversal by U-turn.
Do not drive beyond a Wrong Way or Do Not Enter sign; these often mark a one-way road or expressway ramp.
A One Way sign permits traffic only along the arrow's direction.
A No Parking sign prohibits parking at the signed location.
A center lane marked Left Turn Only may be used only for making a left turn.
A Keep Right sign directs traffic to the right of the island, median or obstruction ahead.
Slower Traffic Keep Right signs help limit weaving and discourage below-normal-speed travel in the left lanes of multilane roads.
A Signal Ahead warning calls for readiness to stop at an approaching traffic signal.
A Reduce Speed Ahead sign warns that a lower-speed zone is approaching.
Stop Ahead warns that a stop sign is approaching.
Yield Ahead warns that a yield sign is approaching.
Divided Highway Begins warns of a median or divider separating one-way traffic lanes and directs drivers to keep right.
Divided Highway Ends warns that a median will no longer separate opposing traffic and directs drivers to keep right.
A Two Way Traffic sign warns of traffic travelling in opposite directions on the current or upcoming road.
An Added Lane sign means entering traffic has its own new lane, so no merge is needed at that point.
An Advisory Exit Speed sign gives the recommended safe speed for leaving a freeway or expressway.
At a Slippery When Wet warning, reduce speed and use caution because wet pavement may be slick.
A Lane Ends warning means the lane will terminate and a merge will be needed.
Do not pass beneath a low-clearance structure if the vehicle is taller than the posted clearance.
A Hill warning indicates a steep downgrade and advises checking the brakes.
A Deer Crossing warning calls for alertness and slowing if a deer is seen.
Deer warnings mark higher-conflict locations, but deer may cross on any Nebraska roadway.
A Horse-Drawn Vehicle sign warns that slow horse-drawn vehicles commonly cross or share the road there.
At a Pedestrian Crossing warning, slow down, yield to people crossing and stop if needed.
A School Advance Crossing sign warns of an upcoming schoolchildren's crosswalk.
A School Crossing sign is placed where children cross; obey the crossing guard's signs.
A Bicycle warning calls for watching for people cycling across the road.
A Reverse Turn sign warns of a sharp turn followed by a turn the other way; the first direction varies with the sign.
A Reverse Curve sign warns of a curve followed by one in the opposite direction; left-first and right-first versions exist.
A Curve warning identifies a gradual bend and calls for slowing to the indicated safe speed.
An advisory-speed plaque adds a recommended speed for the condition described by a diamond warning sign.
A Winding Road warning means several turns or curves lie ahead.
A Crossroad warning identifies a four-way intersection and calls for watching cross traffic.
At a T-intersection warning, the road ends ahead and a right or left turn requires a signal.
The described Sideroad warning identifies a road joining from the right and calls for watching entering vehicles.
At a roundabout warning, reduce speed and yield to vehicles approaching from the left that are already circulating.
A merging-traffic warning from the right calls for adjusting speed and lane position to permit a safe merge.
A Railroad Crossing warning calls for yielding and readiness to stop for an approaching train.
A No Train Horn sign below a railroad warning identifies an established quiet zone.
Green-and-white guide signs provide directions and distances.
Interchange guide diagrams direct drivers toward entrances and exits.
The handbook requires a slow-moving-vehicle emblem on public roads for slow vehicles such as farm equipment travelling at twenty-five miles per hour or less.
Blue-and-white service signs point to facilities such as hospitals, fuel, food and lodging.
A yellow no-passing pennant may stand on the road's left side at the beginning of a no-passing zone.
Nebraska highway reference posts appear at one-mile intervals and help identify a location when assistance is needed.
Accessible parking spaces are reserved for people with the corresponding parking privileges.
Route markers may appear alone or with directional arrows mounted underneath.
Dynamic message signs change their messages to reflect conditions, route traffic or give construction and incident information.
Most dynamic message signs are fixed along freeways, while portable signs can serve work sites, special events or major incidents.
Black lettering on orange warning signs identifies a highway work zone.
Work-zone signs can warn before the work area and also give directions within it.
Stay alert when black-on-orange warnings indicate that a work zone is approaching.
Advance work-zone warnings may call for changing lanes or reducing speed.
Respond to advance work-zone directions early rather than waiting until the last moment and impeding traffic.
Large flashing or sequential arrow panels can direct drivers to particular lanes and warn that roadway ahead is closed.
Most work-zone warning signs have a diamond shape and warn of unusual conditions near the work.
A Flagger warning calls for alertness and readiness to stop where a worker controls traffic.
The handbook describes a flagger in a bright reflective orange vest using a STOP/SLOW paddle to control vehicles.
If a flagger stops you, remain stopped until that flagger directs you to proceed.
Barricades, vertical panels, drums and cones commonly guide vehicles through a work zone.
